title: Gratitude for the ordinary
hook: the people who taught you without a title

segments.voice: Yesterday, gratitude for the scholars, and your line: they were careful. Did you catch yourself checking before you spoke about something you weren't sure of? Day one thousand four hundred twenty-four.

A broom leans against the wall by the door of a mosque. Somebody uses it every evening after the last prayer, and nobody thinks to ask who. Yesterday was for the scholars with names on book spines. Today is for the others. The grandmother who said bismillah before every bite until it stuck. The neighbor who showed a nervous kid where to put their shoes. The friend who answered a clumsy question about Ramadan without making anyone feel foolish. None of them had a title. Some of them taught more than any book did. Today, the people who taught you without a title.
screen: `A BROOM BY THE MOSQUE DOOR.` → `THE GRANDMOTHER, THE NEIGHBOR, THE FRIEND.` → `TEACHERS WITHOUT A TITLE.`

segments.voice: First, thanking people is part of thanking God. In a hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says, in paraphrase: whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah. The two are tied together. Gratitude that skips the person in front of you is not finished. Second, the one who swept the mosque. In Sahih al-Bukhari there is a report about a Black woman, or a man, the narrator was not sure which, who used to sweep the mosque. One day the Prophet noticed she was gone and asked about her. She had died, and no one had told him. In Sahih Muslim's telling, people thought it a small matter. He said, in paraphrase: why didn't you tell me? Show me her grave. And he went to the grave and prayed for her. Nobody had thought her worth a message. He thought her worth a visit. Third, the first teachers of all. The Qur'an asks for thanks to be given to Allah and to one's parents, together, in one breath. And it gives a line to say for them, in Pickthall's translation: "My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little." Care when you were little: that is teaching too, the kind no one writes down. Fourth, the untitled teachers now. The aunt who corrected a verse gently. The coworker who covered a shift so someone could make Friday prayer. The stranger in a mosque who lent a prayer mat and said nothing. The hadith in Abu Dawud puts thanks to them inside thanks to Allah, and the Prophet's walk to a grave shows the honor does not end when they do.
screen: `THANK PEOPLE, AND YOU'VE THANKED GOD.` · `THE ONE WHO SWEPT THE MOSQUE.` · `PARENTS: THE FIRST TEACHERS.` · `THANKS BELONGS TO THEM TOO.`

segments.voice: The practice: thank one. Settle into the sit, and breathe. Let one face come to mind, someone who taught you something about faith, or about being a decent person, and never got called a teacher for it. Remember the moment: what they said, what they did, what it changed. Shape one sentence you could send them: thank you for the time you showed me how to do this. If they have died, and if you pray, you can say the Qur'an's line for parents, or simply ask mercy for them. The bell holds the time.
Gratitude for the ordinary. Thanks owed to the people with no title who taught by doing, because thanking them is part of thanking God. Today's word.

Your line: untitled teachers. Today, send that one sentence to the person you thought of: a text, a call, or a word in person. Tomorrow, humility after learning. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-four.

howItsDone: Muslims say jazakallahu khayran, may Allah reward you with good, to thank someone, and in some families children learn the first words of the faith at home, long before any class.

original.note: Arabic: thanks, gratitude; the opposite in the Qur'an is kufr, ingratitude.

trapdoor: what you thought: gratitude is something between you and God.
what it means: thanking the people who taught you is part of thanking God.
what a scholar hears: Abu Dawud's 'whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah', Bukhari's report of the mosque sweeper, and shukr paired with parents in 31:14.
